_what: THE SAWTOOTH OF BEATING PAIRS — HIS ALGORITHM for the lanes after the sax (SW-15, his words 2026-11-09; RUNNING_LOG §120 · §123). Read by tools/beat_saw.js --roll. Two SHAPES alternate on a lane under its sine, each pair beginning at the unison (the sawtooth); every number rolled in its range, seeded, so the lengths differ. A PACE is seconds for the beating to gain one beat a second (his unit, SW-12).
_A: THE FAST FINISH — a rise at his slower pace for about two-thirds of the way, then much quicker to the peak; the quick leg exists only above his threshold of 5 … 6 beats a second, which the peak's range and the knee at two-thirds guarantee.
_B: THE SLOW LOW ONE — one slower rise that stays under the threshold.
_order: the alternation: A B A B … (his); `startWith` which comes first on a lane — rolled when absent, so the lanes do not all begin alike
_holdS: the peak held before the pair ends (his: 1.8 … 2.6 s, SW-16)
_gapS: the silence between two pairs on a lane: the player breathes, the sine holds (a player lane) or stops (a lane whose sine moves)
_sineMarks: the sine's level by lane, on the ladder (4 dB a mark; ff = 6; 6.25 = ff + 1 dB, his for the sax, SW-14) — the AI's starts for the rest, after Approaching's ear (a low sine louder, a high one softer); his by ear
_noteMarks: the player's written dynamic by lane (the sax f, his SW-17; the crotale mp after Approaching's DEC-66); the AI's starts for the rest
_fadeInMs: the sine's rise from silence (SW-14; the engine's Line in dB)
